source.title: HybriDNA: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba2 Long-Range DNA Language Model
source.authors: Mingqian Ma; Guoqing Liu; Chuan Cao; Pan Deng; Tri Dao; Albert Gu; Peiran Jin; Zhao Yang; Yingce Xia; Renqian Luo; Pipi Hu; Zun Wang; Yuan-Jyue Chen; Haiguang Liu; Tao Qin

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some chart values are not given in text and are recorded as figure only.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a model-size scaling study to DNA pretraining, a different modality from the original language-model scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation-loss curves for three model sizes and a same-size hybrid-versus-pure-Mamba2 loss comparison. It also reports downstream scores for multiple model sizes; those scores are cataloged as V6 results. No numerical loss values or fitted scaling exponents are stated. Other reported results, such as generation scores and computational throughput, do not bear on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: DNA language models at 300M, 3B and 7B, each pretrained on 250B tokens. The paper reports validation loss falling with size (Fig. 3, figure only) and downstream GUE/BEND scores at each size. This is a new modality, so it bears on V5 (loss vs size in DNA) and V6 (downstream vs size). It fits no power law and tests no extrapolation, allocation or fitting choice.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say HybriDNA 'adheres to expected scaling laws', with pretraining loss and downstream performance improving from 300M to 3B and 7B. That claim rests on three loss curves and benchmark tables. There are no fitted exponents, no extrapolation, and no discussion of the downstream categories that do not improve.
record.recipe_differences: DNA next-token pretraining with a hybrid Transformer-Mamba2 model; compares three sizes and reports loss curves rather than fitting the original scaling-law relationships across parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream scores vary by task category; EMP(Y) and CV(V) do not increase monotonically with model size. The paper also reports a separate hybrid-versus-pure-Mamba2 loss comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: At 300M, the hybrid Transformer-Mamba2 model has lower training and validation loss than a pure-Mamba2 model (Fig. A2). The gap size is not stated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter count, the choice of architecture family (adding attention layers to an SSM) changes DNA pretraining loss.

record.problems: Pretraining loss values are shown only in figures, with no numerical values or fitted exponents; the size sweep has three models. Downstream scores are not accompanied by uncertainty estimates, and several categories do not improve monotonically.
record.rows_left_out: Training-loss curves in Fig. 3 were not separately cataloged because the directly relevant loss versions concern held-out/validation loss. The LRB, generative-design, and efficiency results were left out because they do not measure downstream scaling predictability or the claim's loss-scaling relationships.

untested.parts: No power-law fit or exponent. Only parameter count varied (tokens fixed at 250B). Only three sizes, about 1.4 orders of magnitude. Loss values are figure only. No other modalities, repeated-data or transfer regimes.
No fit of downstream score against size or loss. No prediction of held-out runs. No relation to pretraining loss tested.

missing.what: Per-task GUE results where 7B is below 3B. CPD(H) 'all' falls 68.98 to 66.50; PD(H) 'all' falls 89.48 to 88.28; TF(H) task 2 falls 72.21 to 70.42; TF(M) task 2 falls 89.63 to 86.59. Category means hide these drops.

record.verdict_notes: Confounds: pretraining learning rates differ by size (1e-3, 6e-4, 1e-4), as do fine-tuning learning rates. All sizes use the same 250B tokens, so the larger models may be data-limited, which V5 and V1 assume away. The 300M layer count is inconsistent: Table A1 says 24 layers, the footnote says 32. Downstream scores have no uncertainty estimates. V1 is not linked because the data are DNA, not text.

versions.untested_parts: Only parameter-size variation in DNA pretraining is examined; token- and compute-scaling, fitted power-law form, and the several-orders-of-magnitude condition are not established.
No small-run fit is used to predict a substantially larger run.
No fixed-compute-budget allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
The comparison is hybrid versus pure Mamba2 at 300M parameters; there is no broad sweep over depth, width, or other architectural choices, and the size of the loss difference is not reported in text.
Only DNA pretraining is examined. Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning/transfer scaling laws, and quantitative power-law fits are not tested.

The paper reports downstream scores across model sizes, but does not test prediction from pretraining loss, fit a downstream scaling relationship, or evaluate whether that relationship predicts unseen runs.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation are compared across fitting choices or setups.

rows.subject: HybriDNA-300M
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation pretraining loss in the model-size sweep.
rows.note: The authors state that validation loss improves consistently as model size increases; the figure does not provide textual numerical values.
rows.check: DNA pretraining is a non-text modality, so this belongs to V5, not V1. As the smallest model it is the reference point and has no change of its own.

rows.subject: HybriDNA-3B
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation pretraining loss in the model-size sweep.
rows.note: The authors state that validation loss improves consistently as model size increases; the figure does not provide textual numerical values.
rows.check: Link to V5 only, not V1. Fig. 3 and Sec. 4.1 show lower validation loss than 300M, but there are no numbers and no power-law fit.

rows.subject: HybriDNA-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation pretraining loss in the model-size sweep.
rows.note: The authors state that validation loss improves consistently as model size increases; the figure does not provide textual numerical values.
rows.check: Link to V5 only, not V1. The text says loss improves consistently with size; values are figure only and no power-law form is shown.

rows.subject: HybriDNA-300M
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained the hybrid architecture and compared its loss with a same-size model without Transformer layers.
rows.note: The text says the hybrid model has lower loss, but does not state the magnitude needed to assess whether the change is slight.
rows.check: Hybrid vs pure-Mamba2 changes block type (attention vs none), not shape (depth or width) at fixed size. It does not measure what V4 names.

rows.subject: HybriDNA-300M
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained the hybrid architecture and compared its loss with a same-size model without Transformer layers.
rows.note: The text says the hybrid model has lower loss, but does not state the magnitude needed to assess whether the change is slight.
rows.check: Same as A1: an architecture-family comparison, not a shape comparison.

rows.check: Comparator duplicate of A1 for the pure-Mamba2 model. Not a V4 measure.

relationships.reason: Validation loss is lower at each larger size (Fig. 3, Sec. 4.1). Only direction is shown, not power-law form (P2, P3).
relationships.display_finding: Validation loss decreased at each larger model size, without establishing a power-law form.

relationships.condition: GUE PD(H), CPD(H), SS(H), TF(H), TF(M), standard and echo; BEND Chromatin Accessibility and CpG Methylation
relationships.reason: Category means rise with size, though some steps are tiny (e.g. TF(H) 3B to 7B +0.24) (G1–G30, B1–B3, B7–B9).
relationships.display_finding: Category means increased with size, although some gains were small, including a 0.24 increase for TF(H) from 3B to 7B.

relationships.condition: GUE EMP(Y), 3B to 7B, standard and echo
relationships.reason: MCC falls 69.06 to 63.05 (standard) and 68.97 to 65.30 (echo) at the largest size (G31–G36).
relationships.display_finding: MCC fell from 69.06 to 63.05 with standard inference and from 68.97 to 65.30 with echo.

relationships.condition: GUE CV(V) and BEND Histone Modification, 3B to 7B
relationships.reason: Gains stop at 7B: CV flat or slightly down (74.05 to 74.02; 74.88 to 74.30), histone AUROC 0.79 to 0.79 (G37–G42, B4–B6).
relationships.display_finding: CV scores changed from 74.05 to 74.02 and 74.88 to 74.30, while histone modification AUROC stayed at 0.79.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: DNA pretraining at 8,192-token context; 300M, 3B, and 7B models
reader_labels.reason: Validation loss is described as improving with size, but the plotted values are not stated numerically and the paper does not fit or establish a power law (P1–P3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: 300M hybrid model versus 300M pure-Mamba2 model at 8k context
reader_labels.reason: The authors report lower training and validation losses for the hybrid, but the magnitude is unavailable, so the claim that architecture changes loss only slightly cannot be assessed (A1–A4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported validation trend is consistent with lower loss at larger sizes, but does not establish the same power-law form through quantitative fits or exponents (P1–P3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GUE categories PD(H), CPD(H), SS(H), TF(H), and TF(M), and BEND Chromatin Accessibility and CpG Methylation; both standard and echo-embedding GUE settings where shown
reader_labels.reason: Scores generally rise across the tested model sizes in these conditions (G1–G30, B1–B3, B7–B9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GUE EMP(Y) and CV(V); BEND Histone Modification
reader_labels.reason: The largest model reverses the prior gain for EMP(Y) and CV(V), and the BEND histone score does not rise from 3B to 7B (G31–G42, B4–B6).
